hints: Focus on what happens when covalent chlorides meet water, think hydrolysis rather than just dissolving.
Recall that $\text{AlCl}_3$ gives $\text{HCl}$ fumes with water, and $\text{SiCl}_4$ reacts vigorously to give white $\text{SiO}_2$ and $\text{HCl}$.
Check $\text{PCl}_5$ too, it hydrolyses stepwise to release $\text{HCl}$ gas, so count how many of the three give an acidic gas.
walkthrough:
**Spot the reaction type**

All three are chlorides that are readily hydrolysed by water. Hydrolysis of a chloride usually produces the oxide or hydroxide plus $\text{HCl}$.

General idea:
$$\text{chloride + water} \rightarrow \text{oxide / hydroxide + HCl}$$

**Test compound 1, aluminium chloride**

$\text{AlCl}_3$ hydrolyses in warm water to aluminium hydroxide and hydrogen chloride gas, which is acidic and forms white fumes.

$$\text{AlCl}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Al(OH)}_3 + 3\text{HCl}$$

**Test compound 2, silicon tetrachloride**

$\text{SiCl}_4$ is a classic vigorously hydrolysed liquid, giving solid silicon dioxide and hydrogen chloride gas.

$$\text{SiCl}_4 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{SiO}_2 + 4\text{HCl}$$

**Test compound 3, phosphorus pentachloride**

$\text{PCl}_5$ also hydrolyses with a little warm water, first to $\text{POCl}_3$ and then further, releasing $\text{HCl}$ at each stage.

$$\text{PCl}_5 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{POCl}_3 + 2\text{HCl}$$

**Conclude the combination**

Since 1, 2 and 3 all evolve $\text{HCl}$, which is an acidic gas that turns damp blue litmus red, the correct combination is 1, 2 and 3 together.

options.A: Correct. All three hydrolyse to release HCl gas. Aluminium chloride gives Al(OH)3 + HCl, silicon tetrachloride gives SiO2 + HCl, and phosphorus pentachloride gives POCl3 / H3PO4 + HCl. HCl is acidic.
options.B: Incorrect. This combination leaves out phosphorus pentachloride. Students sometimes think only Period 3 metal and Group 4 chlorides hydrolyse, but PCl5 hydrolyses very readily to give HCl as well.
options.C: Incorrect. This combination leaves out aluminium chloride. Students sometimes think AlCl3 just dissolves to give a neutral solution, but with a little warm water it hydrolyses to give HCl fumes.
options.D: Incorrect. This suggests only one compound gives an acidic gas. All the covalent / polar chlorides here hydrolyse, so limiting it to one misses the vigorous hydrolysis of SiCl4 and PCl5.
